## Requirements Extracted

1. Checked scoped clauses explicitly declare trigger, response, correlation key, clock, bound, endpoint, identity, and source.
2. Repeated triggers create independent obligations; matching responses discharge eligible obligations.
3. Only admitted transitions of the captured operation advance its clock, including self-loops.
4. Responses are accepted at trigger and inclusive deadline coordinates; violations are irreversible.
5. Model, incremental, and offline evaluation share passive obligation semantics.
6. Checked proofs connect existing Property meaning, scoped projection, execution, and portable lowering.
7. Deliberate closure and incomplete prefixes retain different outcomes.
8. Unsupported forms reject the whole requested lowering with source-owned diagnostics.
9. Command submission remains separate from confirmed Target-owned transitions.
10. Evidence admission is bounded, causal, deterministic, atomic, and preserves exact support.
11. Query validity independently reports satisfiability, exercise, answer, completeness, policies, and limits.
12. Terminal composition, deterministic selection, Exact Replay, and nonvacuous witness selection remain sound.
13. Temporal notation and typed constructors have identical canonical meaning and source-local misuse diagnostics.
14. Behavior forms preserve existing constraints, ordering/adjacency distinctions, exactness, and fingerprints.
15. Scoped lowering produces closed, versioned Case 1.0 capability data, admitted before Driver I/O.
16. Lean/Go and incremental/offline qualification cover deadlines, partial evidence, correlation, and immutable outcomes.
17. Public Prepare/Run exercises a deterministic non-cancellation scoped Case while preserving Nexus success integration.
18. Negative evidence, interruption, cleanup failure, concurrent Runs, and tenfold loads preserve bounded failure and prior proof.
19. Compatibility, trust audits, generation/staleness checks, builds, lints, and functional validation have recorded evidence.
20. Documentation describes ownership, authoring, operational limits, and explicitly deferred cancellation.
